what: Per-endpoint response KEY SETS for every grandfathered Class B.2 endpoint+method pair in
ALIGNMENT.md § 'Current Class B inventory', recorded from the wire by booting a real
server.mjs and probing it. Values are never recorded — only key paths, the HTTP status and
the content-type — so uptime, timestamps and counters cannot make this file flap.
This is the mechanism that replaced the ADR 0012 prose grep (#346). The grep could only ever
see additions whose author WROTE the marker; a field added with no marker produced 'none this
cycle', which is a green result for the exact case it was least able to see. This file is
produced from what the server actually returns, so it does not depend on anyone writing
anything. Its git history IS the per-release record of how B.2 surface grew:
Generated and checked by scripts/b2-key-snapshot.mjs. The suite fails on any difference.
Read notCovered below before treating a green run as coverage.
regenerate: node scripts/b2-key-snapshot.mjs --write   (then state the field names in the PR body AND the CHANGELOG — ADR 0012 condition 5)

keyPathNotation.a.b: object member b of object member a
keyPathNotation.a[]: a is an ARRAY; recorded even when empty, so array->object is visible
keyPathNotation.a[].b: member b of some element of array a (union over all elements)
keyPathNotation.present-but-null: IN the key set — /health's instanceName ships as "" rather than being omitted (#327) precisely so consumers can tell null from absent, and this preserves that

notCovered: TYPE changes under an unchanged key path. A key set records names, not types: string -> number under the same name is invisible. Container changes ARE visible (object <-> scalar adds/removes children; array <-> object adds/removes the '[]' marker).
RENAMES, as renames. A rename appears as one '-' and one '+'; the test fails, which is the point, but it cannot tell a rename from an unrelated removal plus an unrelated addition.

Shapes that only exist under a NON-DEFAULT configuration. The fixture pins the config that decides shape (see scripts/b2-key-snapshot.mjs § makeB2Fixture). Known conditional shapes NOT recorded here: CLAUDE_TUI_MODE=true replaces /health's 4-key spawn block with a 3-key variant that has no 'reason', and gives tui.pool an object instead of null; CLAUDE_SKIP_PERMISSIONS=true makes config.allowedTools a string, so config.allowedTools[] disappears.

Responses to a NON-LOCALHOST caller. Probes come from 127.0.0.1, where server.mjs treats every caller as admin, so the 401/403 bodies on these endpoints are unreachable here — as is the omission of /health's anonymousKey, which is sent to remote callers only when PROXY_ADVERTISE_ANON_KEY=1.

ERROR and validation responses. Only the success path of each pair is recorded. PATCH /settings's errors[] array exists only when an update is rejected; the 400/404/413 bodies on the key and settings endpoints are likewise absent.

/status's plan sub-shape. The fixture has no OAuth credentials by construction (otherwise npm test would make a real billed call to api.anthropic.com), so plan is recorded as a scalar error string. With live credentials it is an object.

/dashboard's body. It is HTML, and a key set is not defined for it — hence keys: null. It is RECORDED rather than skipped: status and content-type are still asserted, so if it ever starts returning JSON the test fires.
/usage. It is the Hybrid endpoint (ALIGNMENT.md § Hybrid note), not a row in the B.2 inventory table, and its synthesis layer cannot be probed without a live Anthropic wire call.

Element keys of sessions[] on /health and /sessions. They are empty in every run because nothing in server.mjs ever writes the sessions Map (declared server.mjs:965; only .delete and .clear are ever called on it). The array is unreachable, not under-probed.

Keys of JSON-parseable /logs entries. Only entries[].raw is recorded, because that fallback object is the one part of an entry server.mjs constructs; a JSON line passes through verbatim, so its keys belong to whatever wrote the log, not to the endpoint.
Response HEADERS beyond the content-type family.

AUTHORIZATION. This says the surface changed. It never says whether the change was allowed. ADR 0012 condition 5 — the marker and the field names in the PR body and the CHANGELOG — is still a human obligation, and this file is the thing that makes forgetting it detectable rather than the thing that satisfies it.
